blocks.text: 1. Image Captioning

blocks.alt: An input image goes through a CNN encoder and language decoder to produce a caption

blocks.text: Instance Segmentation, the previous topic, produced precise, per-object pixel masks. Image Captioning shifts from spatial tasks to describing an image's content in natural language, a genuinely different output type explored throughout this topic.
It produces a genuinely full, grammatical sentence describing an image, rather than labels or masks, a genuinely distinctive task covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Shift In Output Type

This connects back to every task already covered throughout this module. Image Classification, Object Detection, Semantic and Instance Segmentation all produce genuinely structured, non-linguistic output.
Image Captioning genuinely produces free-form natural language instead, a genuinely fundamental shift in output type from every prior task already covered in this module.
3. Two Modalities Combined

blocks.alt: Vision features and a language model combine for captioning

blocks.text: A genuinely important, distinctive characteristic connects back to image data, already covered throughout this course. Image Captioning genuinely combines visual understanding with language generation, two genuinely different kinds of data working together.

This combination of two genuinely different modalities is a genuinely important theme that reappears throughout Multimodal Deep Learning, covered later in this course, with Image Captioning standing as one of its genuinely earliest, clearest examples.

blocks.text: 4. Recapping The Encoder-Decoder Pattern

blocks.alt: An image passes through an encoder and decoder to produce words

blocks.text: This connects back to the encoder-decoder structure, already covered in Semantic Segmentation. Image Captioning genuinely uses a similar encoder-decoder pattern, but with a genuinely different decoder than that earlier topic used.

An image encoder extracts features, already covered throughout the CNN module, while a genuinely different, language-producing decoder generates the caption, rather than the pixel-level decoder already covered in Semantic Segmentation.
5. Sequential Word Generation

blocks.alt: Words are generated one after another in sequence

blocks.text: A genuinely important structural detail connects forward to Recurrent Neural Networks, covered later in this course. Captions genuinely get generated one word at a time, each word conditioned on the image and the words already produced.

This genuinely sequential process, explored in complete depth in that later module, is exactly what makes Image Captioning genuinely different from the single-shot outputs already covered throughout most of this module.
6. A Preview Of Attention

blocks.alt: A decoder uses attention to focus on the relevant image region

blocks.text: A genuinely important, related concept connects forward to Attention Mechanism, covered later in this course. Modern captioning systems genuinely let the decoder focus on genuinely different image regions while generating each word.

This genuinely valuable capability, explored in complete depth in that later module, lets the model genuinely look at the relevant part of the image for each word it produces, rather than relying on one fixed, static summary.

blocks.text: 7. The Evaluation Challenge

blocks.alt: A generated caption is compared against reference captions

blocks.text: This connects back to Evaluation Metrics, already covered in its own module. Evaluating captions is genuinely harder than evaluating a single label or box, already covered as the simpler evaluation cases throughout earlier topics.
Multiple genuinely different captions can all be genuinely correct descriptions of the exact same image, a genuinely real challenge that plain Accuracy, already covered, cannot meaningfully handle.
8. A Brief Mention Of Specialized Metrics

A genuinely important, real practical response connects back to the evaluation challenge, already covered in this topic. Specialized metrics compare a generated caption against multiple genuinely valid human-written reference captions.
This genuinely practical approach directly addresses the many-valid-answers problem already covered in the previous section, rather than expecting an exact, single correct match.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Image Captioning Is Genuinely Valuable

blocks.alt: Needing a text description of an image points toward using image captioning

blocks.text: Accessibility tools helping visually impaired users understand image content is a direct case where Image Captioning, already covered in this topic, directly provides genuinely natural, descriptive text.

This connects forward to Multimodal Deep Learning, covered later in this course, combining vision and language. Image Captioning, already covered, is genuinely one of the clearest, earliest examples of this combination.

blocks.text: 11. Computer Vision Tasks: Progress Recap

items: Image Captioning generates a natural language sentence describing an image's content.
It produces free-form language, a fundamental shift from the structured outputs of every prior task.
It combines two modalities: visual understanding and language generation.
It uses an encoder-decoder pattern, with a language-producing decoder generating the caption.
Captions get generated one word at a time, each conditioned on the image and prior words.
Modern systems use Attention to focus on relevant image regions while generating each word.
Evaluating captions is genuinely harder, since multiple different captions can all be correct.
Specialized metrics compare a generated caption against multiple valid human-written references.
Next up: Pose Estimation, which locates the specific keypoints of a body within an image.
